questions.prompt: How does a plain bearing reduce shaft friction?
options: Gear teeth mesh with the shaft
questions.explanation: A plain bearing supports a sliding shaft surface with lubrication; antifriction bearings use rolling elements.

reviewCue.text: Review C210 Mechanical Power Sys.pdf, slide 60. A plain bearing supports a sliding shaft surface with lubrication; antifriction bearings use rolling elements.
reviewCue.excerpt:
The Function of a Bearing
A solid(PLAIN) bearing uses lubricant to reduce friction between the shaft and the 
bearing. The shaft rotates inside the bearing with a lubricant layer that separates it from 
the bearing's metal surface. A solid bearing is also known as a "fluid film bearing."
Solid bearings are lubricated by a grease or oil fitting in the bearing housing. 
Machines that have many bearings often have an “AUTOMATIC LUBRICATION SYSTEM”   
THAT SUPPLIES LUBRICANT TO MANY LOCATIONS LIKE BEARINGS IN AN AUTOMOBILE ENGINE.
60

reviewCue.excerpt:
Three Types of Bearing Loads 
Radial or side loads act in a direction that is perpendicular 
to the axis of the shaft. Radial bearings carry radial loads 
and some small thrust loads. An example is the shaft shown 
here. The weight of the shaft and any attached hubs or 
gears creates a force that pulls downward on the radial 
bearings.
Combination loads with both a radial load and a thrust load 
are fairly common. One example is the robot body like the 
one shown here. When the body rotates, the weight of the 
machine creates a radial load along with the thrust load.
Force
Thrust or axial loads act in a direction parallel to the shaft 
axis and opposite to the direction of force. These thrust 
bearings can carry some small axial load. As the screw 
shown here drives the load, it creates a thrust load on the 
shaft in the opposite direction.

reviewCue.excerpt:
How Bearings Are Positioned to Support a Load
For radial loads, use at least two bearings to 
secure the position of the shaft. Place the 
load between the two bearings or overhang 
it. An overhung load is also called a 
cantilever load.
CANTILEVER LOAD
Machines like this electric motor have
built-in bearings mounted externally. All electric 
motors have two bearings, one on each side of the 
housing to support the motor's rotor and shaft. They 
also support an external radial load, allowing other 
parts such as gears and hubs to be attached without 
extra  external bearings.
Thrust loads only need one bearing. Place this bearing anywhere on the shaft in a 
way such that it can counteract the direction of the thrust load. This bearing must 
have some shelf or set screw to stop slippage

reviewCue.text: Review C210 Mechanical Power Sys.pdf, slide 99. Backlash is related to the difference between tooth thickness and the mating tooth space. It is checked with the specified measuring procedure.
reviewCue.excerpt:
Backlash
Backlash is the difference between the thickness of a tooth and the width of the tooth space 
where the pitch circles touch.
Most gears need some backlash built into them to allow them to mesh smoothly and allow space 
for  lubrication between the gears.
There are standard look-up tables to determine this distance. It is created by making the tooth 
thickness slightly smaller than the tooth width and adjusting the center-to-center distance of the 
gears. 
Backlash is typically a few thousandths of an inch.
If adjusted correctly, the pitch circles are meeting 
at one point, a tangent.
